mainEntity.name: Are these written to sell me something?

acceptedAnswer.text:
They are on a business website, so they are not disinterested. What they are not is written to make a job sound harder or more urgent than it is.

The test is simple enough: each guide tells you at least one thing that costs us work. The gutter frequency guide says most houses need it less often than the industry line suggests, and the cost guide tells you which pricing model to avoid.

Because those are the five questions that actually come up, and a resources section with forty thin articles is worse than one with five useful ones.

More will be added when there is a question worth answering, not on a content schedule.

mainEntity.name: Can I use this information to do the job myself?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Yes, and for some of it you should. Clearing a single storey gutter you can reach safely from a ladder, with somebody footing it, is a reasonable Saturday.

What the guides will not do is talk you into going onto a two storey roof or up against glass on a ladder. Most of the serious injuries in this trade are falls, and they happen to people doing a quick job.
The method and the physics do not change. Where a guide carries anything that can date, it says so in the text rather than wearing a freshness badge at the top.
